Generated Narrative: CodeSystem DAKComponents

This case-sensitive code system http://smart.who.int/trust/CodeSystem/DAKComponents defines the following codes:

CodeDisplayDefinition
health-interventions-and-recommendations Health Interventions & RecommendationsRelevant health interventions and recommendations from the WHO guideline and guidance. To inform DAK scope.
generic-personas Generic PersonasRoles, responsibilities, and essential interventions performed by targeted personas. Example for human centered design.
user-scenarios User ScenariosBrief narrative description of how the targeted personas may engage with the digital system. Example for human centered design.
generic-business-processes-and-workflows Business Processes & WorkflowsGeneric workflows representing clinical and non-clinical processes. To inform when data is collected and used & required features.
core-data-elements Core Data ElementsData elements, used for clinical decision-making, indicators, and other data needs. To inform data collection forms and L3 interoperability requirements.
decision-support-logic Decision Support LogicDecision tables representing counselling and treatment algorithms, and any other logic used to determine workflow paths or clinical actions.
scheduling-logic Scheduling LogicDecision tables representing scheduling logic according to care plans. Previously combined with decision support logic. Not yet a field of its own in WHO's DAK logical model.
programme-indicators Indicators & MonitoringIndicators for reporting & monitoring with numerator, denominator of data elements. Linking person centered data to aggregate.
functional-and-non-functional-requirements Functional & Non-functional RequirementsA non-exhaustive list of key functions and non-functional requirements for a digital tracking and decision support system. To inform system features.
test-scenarios Test ScenariosTest data and scenarios to check a system against the other nine components. A test harness to run them.

name: DAKComponents
title: DAK components
description: The ten components of a WHO SMART Guidelines Digital Adaptation Kit (DAK), as smart-base's DAK document kind lists them (smart-base document-kinds/dak.json). A Trust Domain's use cases point at these components. Move to smart-base once its DAK logical model publishes a code system for them.
